mainTopic: An אשרה: sitting in its shade, walking under it, and planting beneath it (זה וזה גורם)
overview: The משנה teaches rules about an אשרה, a tree that people worship. You may not sit in its shade, though if you did you stay טהור. You may not walk under it, and if you did you become טמא. רבי יוחנן explains that the ban on sitting reaches even the farther shade (צל צילה). A second version says the חידוש is that a person stays טהור even in the main shade. Walking under the tree makes a person טמא because some idolatrous offering is surely lying under it, and רבי יהודה בן בתירא learns from a פסוק that such an offering makes things טמא in a tent, like a dead body. For a tree hanging over a public road, you may pass under it if there is no other way; רב ששת still hurried past because an אדם חשוב must be extra careful. A new משנה discusses planting vegetables under an אשרה, and the גמרא asks whether רבי יוסי and the רבנן argue about זה וזה גורם. It resolves a clash with another משנה either by swapping the names or by saying the leaves' benefit is cancelled by the shade's harm. It then starts to question whether רבי יוסי really forbids זה וזה גורם, citing a teaching about ערלה, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה: shade of an אשרה and passing beneath it
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives four rules about an אשרה: two about sitting in its shade and two about walking under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: A person should not sit in the shade of an אשרה, but if he did sit there he remains טהור. He should not pass under it, and if he did pass under it he is טמא. If the tree was 'robbing the public' (its branches stick out over public space) and he passed under it, he is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lays down the rules for sitting in an אשרה's shade and for walking underneath it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the shade is forbidden from the start, but it does not make a person טמא. Walking under the tree is also forbidden, and this one does make him טמא. The exception is a tree whose branches reach over public property: walking under it there leaves him טהור, though the משנה does not give the reason here.

keyTerms.meaning: A tree that people worship as an idol
Literally 'robbing the public': its branches hang over public property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of rules. 'Do not sit' and 'do not pass' tell you what is forbidden. 'טהור' and 'טמא' tell you what happens to a person who already did it. Sitting is forbidden but leaves him טהור; passing under is forbidden and makes him טמא.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One may not sit in its shade,
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the אשרה, the worshipped tree that the earlier משניות were discussing.

phrases.english: but if he sat — he is pure,
and one may not pass beneath it,
and if he passed — he is impure.
If it was robbing the public
phrases.notes: He means its branches stretch out over public ground, like a street.

phrases.english: and he passed beneath it — he is pure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sitting in an אשרה's shade is forbidden but leaves a person טהור. Passing beneath it is forbidden and makes him טמא. Passing beneath branches that hang over public space leaves him טהור.

steps.title: Why teach that one may not sit in its shade? It is obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's first rule and asks why it needs to be said at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: 'One may not sit in its shade.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's first rule as too obvious to need saying. This sets up an answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in the shade means getting direct benefit from an idol, and that is clearly forbidden. So the גמרא wants to know what new lesson (חידוש) the משנה is adding.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
It is obvious! Why say it?

phrases.english: GEMARA:
'One may not sit in its shade.'
That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה's first clause is needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Benefiting from an idol's shade is clearly forbidden, so the clause seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even the farther shade is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה, quoting רבי יוחנן, answers that the clause is needed for צל צילה, the weaker shade farther from the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The rule was only needed for the 'shade of its shade.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the משנה is forbidding even the weak, far-off shade, not just the main shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two zones of shade. The main shade reaches as far as the tree's height. The farther, weaker shade reaches beyond that. Forbidding the main shade would be obvious, so the משנה's חידוש is that even the farther shade is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: The shade of its shade: the weaker shade beyond the tree's height

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is necessary only for the shade of its shade.
phrases.notes: This is the farther shade, past the distance of the tree's own height.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the clause to a less obvious case (צל צילה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The clause only forbids the main shade, which is obvious
steps.terutzMaskana: The clause teaches that even the farther shade is forbidden

steps.title: Does this imply that the main shade makes a person impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests a possible inference from רבי יוחנן's answer: does the main shade (צל קומתה) make a person טמא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that imply that if he sat in the shade of its height, he is טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוחנן's answer leads to a surprising conclusion. This sets up the response in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the clause 'if he sat, he is טהור' was said about the farther shade, maybe the main shade is different, and sitting there makes a person טמא. The גמרא checks whether that reading is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The shade of its height: the main shade, within the tree's height

phrases.english: By implication, in the shade of its height,
if he sat — he is impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible implication from the answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether sitting in the main shade makes a person טמא

steps.title: No: even the main shade leaves a person pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. A person is טהור even in the main shade; the חידוש is only that sitting is forbidden even in the farther shade.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Even in the shade of its height, if he sat there he is טהור. What the משנה teaches us is that he may not sit even in the shade of its shade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers no. Sitting in any of the shade leaves a person טהור, and the משנה's new point is only about what is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's answer was about the 'do not sit' part of the משנה, not the טהור part. So nothing changes about טומאה: both zones of shade leave a person טהור. The חידוש is simply how far the ban on sitting reaches.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: Version 1: 'do not sit' reaches even the farther shade (צל צילה). Sitting in either shade leaves a person טהור.

phrases.english: No, for even regarding the shade of its height as well,
if he sat — he is pure,
and this is what it teaches us,
that even in the shade of its shade he may not sit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed inference
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even the main shade leaves a person טהור; the חידוש is that sitting is forbidden even in the farther shade.

steps.title: Second version: why teach that one who sat is pure?
steps.stepSummary: Some attach רבי יוחנן's teaching to the later clause, 'if he sat, he is טהור,' and ask why that clause is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach this discussion on the later clause: 'if he sat, he is טהור.' Isn't that obvious?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of the discussion. In it, the 'obvious' question is aimed at the טהור clause, and the answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sitting in shade does not seem like something that would make a person טמא. So this version asks why the משנה needs to tell us that he stays טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who teach it…

phrases.english: There are those who teach it on the latter clause:
'But if he sat, he is pure.'
Is that not obvious?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restarts the discussion as a second version on a different clause
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is no reason sitting in shade would make a person טמא, so stating that he is טהור seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: needed for the main shade
steps.stepSummary: In this version, רבי יוחנן says the טהור clause is needed for the main shade (צל קומתה).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: It was only needed for the shade of its height.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the חידוש is that a person stays טהור even in the main, closest shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might have thought that the main shade, close to the tree, is strong enough to make a person טמא. The משנה teaches that even there he stays טהור.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
that Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
It is necessary only for the shade of its height.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of the second version
steps.terutzResolutionType: Placing the clause in the stronger case (צל קומתה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Sitting in the main shade might make a person טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in the main shade, he remains טהור

steps.title: Does this imply that one may sit in the farther shade from the start?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests an inference: if the clause is about the main shade, is the farther shade permitted even from the start?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that imply that in the shade of its shade, he may sit there even from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא checks whether the second version leads to a surprising leniency. The response comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the 'do not sit... but if he sat' discussion is about the main shade, maybe the farther shade is not forbidden at all. The גמרא checks whether that is right.

keyTerms.meaning: From the start, before acting (as opposed to after the fact)

phrases.english: By implication, in the shade of its shade
he may sit even from the start?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible implication from the second version's answer
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether sitting in the farther shade is permitted from the start

steps.title: No: the point is only that even the main shade leaves him pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the inference. The משנה's point is only that a person who sat even in the main shade stays טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What the משנה teaches us is that even in the shade of its height, if he sat there he is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers no. The farther shade is not being permitted; the only lesson is that a person stays טהור even in the main shade.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יוחנן's teaching is about the טהור clause only. It says nothing new about where sitting is allowed. Since the חידוש is that even the main shade does not make a person טמא, nothing here suggests the farther shade is permitted from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: Version 2: the חידוש is that a person who sat even in the main shade (צל קומתה) stays טהור. In both versions, a person who sat in the shade is טהור.

phrases.english: No, this is what it teaches us:
that even regarding the shade of its height,
if he sat — he is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proposed inference
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The clause only teaches that a person stays טהור even in the main shade; it does not permit sitting in the farther shade.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both versions agree that a person who sat in the shade is טהור. They differ only on which clause of the משנה רבי יוחנן's teaching explains.

steps.title: Why does passing under the tree make a person impure?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that passing under an אשרה makes one טמא and asks for the reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one may not pass under the אשרה, and if he did, he is טמא. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks why passing under the tree makes someone טמא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tree itself is not normally a source of טומאה. So the גמרא wants to know what under the tree could make a person who walks there טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: He will pass beneath it (the tree)

phrases.english: And one may not pass beneath it,
and if he passed, he is impure.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sitting-in-the-shade lines of the משנה to its next line about passing under the tree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason passing under an אשרה makes one טמא.

steps.title: There is surely an idolatrous offering under the tree
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that there is certainly some leftover idolatrous offering under the tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is impossible that there is no idolatrous offering under it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: people bring offerings to this tree, so we assume some offering is lying underneath it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה does not come from the tree. It comes from the offering assumed to be under it, and walking under the same tree covering it makes the person טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought to an idol

phrases.english: It is impossible that there is not
an idolatrous offering [beneath it].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: We assume an idolatrous offering lies under the tree, and that offering is what makes the passer-by טמא.

steps.title: Whose opinion is this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא holds that an idolatrous offering makes a person under the same covering טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא this משנה follows. This sets up the next step, where it names him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not everyone agrees that an idolatrous offering spreads טומאה to whatever is under the same covering. So the משנה must follow a specific opinion, and the גמרא wants to find it.

phrases.english: Whose opinion is it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 11's answer and asks who holds that view.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that an idolatrous offering makes things טמא through a covering.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who compares the offering to a dead body
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who learns from a פסוק that an idolatrous offering makes things טמא in a tent, like a dead body.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יהודה בן בתירא, as a ברייתא teaches: How do we know an idolatrous offering makes things טמא in a tent? The פסוק says, 'They attached themselves to בעל פעור and ate the offerings of the dead.' Just as a dead body makes things טמא in a tent, so does an idolatrous offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא names רבי יהודה בן בתירא and brings his source from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls offerings to בעל פעור 'offerings of the dead,' linking them to a dead body. A dead body makes everything under the same covering טמא (טומאת אהל), so the idolatrous offering does too. That is why walking under the tree makes a person טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes things impure through a covering, like a tent

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה בן בתירא, an idolatrous offering is treated like a dead body: it makes everything under the same covering טמא. That is why passing under the אשרה makes a person טמא.

phrases.english: It is the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
From where do we know that an idolatrous offering
transmits impurity in a tent?
phrases.notes: "In a tent" means anything under the same roof or covering as it becomes טמא.

phrases.english: As it is stated:
"And they joined themselves to Baal Peor
and ate the offerings of the dead."
phrases.notes: תהלים 106:28

phrases.english: Just as a corpse transmits impurity in a tent,

phrases.aramaic: אַף תִּקְרוֹבֶת עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מְטַמֵּא בְּאֹהֶל.
phrases.english: so too, an idolatrous offering transmits impurity in a tent.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא הִיא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by naming the תנא and quoting his source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who learns from תהלים 106:28 that an idolatrous offering makes things טמא in a tent, like a dead body.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן בתירא, based on תהלים 106:28

steps.title: Tree over a public road: 'passed' or 'may pass'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says one who passes under a tree hanging over a public road is טהור. The גמרא asks whether this only applies after the fact or whether passing there is allowed from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if the tree was 'robbing the public' and he passed under it, he is טהור. They asked: does it mean 'if he passed' (only after the fact) or 'he may pass' (even from the start)?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of a tree over a public road and asks how to read its wording. This sets up the answers in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's word 'עבר' could mean 'if he already passed,' which suggests he should avoid it from the start. It could also simply describe passing that is allowed. The question is whether walking under it is allowed לכתחילה or only acceptable בדיעבד.

keyTerms.meaning: Robbing the public (hanging over a public road)
A question was asked among the scholars
'Passed' (after the fact) or 'passes' (allowed from the start)?

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree the person is טהור. The question is only whether he may go under the tree in the first place.

phrases.english: If it was robbing the public
phrases.notes: The tree's branches hang over a public road, so it "steals" space from the public.

phrases.english: and one passed beneath it, he is pure.
A question was raised before them:
Does it mean "passed" or "may pass"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה: a tree hanging over a public road.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether passing under an אשרה over a public road is allowed לכתחילה or only acceptable בדיעבד.

steps.title: Two answers: 'may pass' and 'if he passed'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר in the name of חזקיה says one may pass from the start. רבי יוחנן says the משנה only means after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר said in the name of חזקיה: one may pass. רבי יוחנן said: 'if he passed' (only after the fact).
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים give opposite answers to the question. One allows passing from the start, and the other allows it only after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חזקיה's view reads the משנה as fully allowing it. רבי יוחנן reads it as 'if he already did, he is טהור,' but he should not go there to begin with. At this point they look like they disagree.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה אָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar said in the name of Chizkiya:
One may pass.
And Rabbi Yochanan said: "If he passed."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives two answers to the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חזקיה says passing is allowed לכתחילה. רבי יוחנן says it is acceptable only בדיעבד.

steps.title: No real disagreement: it depends on whether there is another road
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the two opinions do not argue. If there is another road, one should not pass under the tree. If there is no other road, one may.
steps.simpleTranslation: They do not disagree. One case is where there is another road; the other case is where there is no other road.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the two אמוראים are talking about different situations, so there is no real argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן ('only if he passed') speaks about a case where another route exists, so one should avoid the tree. חזקיה ('may pass') speaks about a case where this is the only route, so passing is allowed from the start.
steps.whatToRemember: Under a tree of עבודה זרה hanging over a public road: if there is another way, do not go under it (but if you did, you are טהור). If there is no other way, you may go under it.

phrases.english: And they do not disagree.
This is where there is another way,
phrases.notes: This fits רבי יוחנן: with another road available, use it and avoid the tree.

phrases.english: and that is where there is no other way.
phrases.notes: This fits חזקיה: with no other road, he may pass under the tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the apparent argument from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each opinion is about a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked like חזקיה and רבי יוחנן argue about whether one may pass under the tree.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where there is another road, one should avoid it. Where there is no other road, one may pass even from the start.

steps.title: רב ששת asks to be rushed past the tree
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tells his attendant to make him run when they reach the אשרה over the road.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to his attendant: When you get there, make me run.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story about רב ששת. He asked his attendant to rush him past the spot where an אשרה shaded the road.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story connects to the rule just taught in step 16 about walking under an אשרה. Running suggests רב ששת wanted to spend as little time under it as possible. The next step will ask what case this was.

keyTerms.meaning: His attendant, the person who served him
Make me run, rush me along

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said to his attendant:
When you reach there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the spot where the אשרה tree hung over the road.

phrases.english: "make me run."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real-life story about the rule of walking under an אשרה that was just settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב ששת asked to be rushed past an אשרה over the road.

steps.title: Either way, running makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case was. If there was no other road, walking was allowed anyway. If there was another road, running would not make it allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was the case? If there was no other road, why say "make me run"? It is fully permitted. And if there was another road, does saying "make me run" make it permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the story using the rule from step 16. Neither possible case seems to explain why רב ששת asked to run.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 16 taught that walking under the tree is allowed if there is no other road, and not allowed if there is one. Under that rule, running adds nothing. If walking was allowed, running is not needed. If walking was forbidden, running does not fix it, because he still passes under the tree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the details?

phrases.english: What was the case?
If there was no other road,
why do I need "make me run"?
It is completely permitted!
And if there was another road,
when he says "make me run," is it then permitted?
phrases.notes: He still passes under the tree, even if he goes fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי דְּלֵיכָּא דִּירְכָּא אַחֲרִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the story of step 17 using the rule from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's request to run past the אשרה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided question: in one case running is not needed, and in the other case running does not help.

steps.title: An important person is different
steps.stepSummary: There really was no other road. Still, an important person like רב ששת should be stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, there was no other road, but an important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the case had no other road, so walking was allowed. רב ששת ran anyway because an important person must hold himself to a higher standard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא picks the first side of the question. The basic rule stays the same: with no other road, walking is allowed. People learn from what an important person does, so he must act in a way that will not be misunderstood. Running past the tree shows he is not treating it lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in fact. It signals the answer picks one of the options

steps.whatToRemember: With no other road, anyone may pass under an אשרה. An אדם חשוב should still hurry past so others do not learn the wrong thing from him.

phrases.english: Really, it was where there was no other road,
and an important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the question and adds a special rule for an important person
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Running seemed pointless in either case.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was no other road. רב ששת ran only because an אדם חשוב must be extra careful.

steps.title: משנה: planting vegetables under an אשרה
steps.stepSummary: Vegetables may be planted under an אשרה in the rainy season but not in summer. Lettuce may never be planted there. רבי יוסי forbids vegetables even in the rainy season, because the falling leaves fertilize them.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may plant vegetables under it in the rainy season but not in the summer. Lettuce may be planted neither in the summer nor in the rainy season. רבי יוסי says: Not even vegetables in the rainy season, because the leaves fall on them and become fertilizer for them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה teaches when one may plant under an אשרה. The question is whether the vegetables would benefit from the forbidden tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In summer the tree's shade helps vegetables grow, so planting there means benefiting from the אשרה. In the rainy season the shade does not help, so the תנא קמא allows it. Lettuce always gains from shade, so it is always forbidden. רבי יוסי adds that in the rainy season the fallen leaves act as fertilizer, which is also a benefit.
steps.confusionAlert: Here וְהַחֲזֵירִין means a kind of lettuce, not pigs.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One may plant vegetables under it
in the rainy season,
but not in the summer,
and lettuce,

phrases.aramaic: לֹא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה וְלֹא בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים.
phrases.english: not in the summer and not in the rainy season.
Rabbi Yosei says:
not even vegetables in the rainy season,
because the leaves fall on them
and become fertilizer for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about planting under an אשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Planting under an אשרה is forbidden when the plants benefit from it. The תנא קמא and רבי יוסי argue about vegetables in the rainy season.

steps.title: Is this an argument about זה וזה גורם?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יוסי holds that when a forbidden cause and a permitted cause work together, the result is forbidden, while the רבנן hold it is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that רבי יוסי holds: when this and that cause it, it is forbidden; and the רבנן say: when this and that cause it, it is permitted?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the argument in the משנה comes from a bigger principle called זה וזה גורם. This question sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The vegetables grow from two causes together: the permitted soil and the forbidden leaves of the אשרה. If רבי יוסי forbids them, maybe he holds that a mix of causes makes the result forbidden. Then the רבנן would hold that it stays permitted. The גמרא is checking whether this is really what they argue about.

keyTerms.meaning: Is this to say? It opens a suggested reading
Both this and that cause it: a permitted cause and a forbidden cause working together
The Sages, here the first opinion in the משנה

steps.whyThisMatters: זה וזה גורם is a major principle for any result produced by both a permitted and a forbidden source.

phrases.english: GEMARA:
Is this to say that Rabbi Yosei holds:
when this and that cause it, it is forbidden,
phrases.notes: "This and that" here means the permitted soil and the forbidden leaves, both helping the plant grow.

phrases.english: and the Rabbis say:
when this and that cause it, it is permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether the argument in the משנה of step 20 is based on a general principle.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוסי and the רבנן disagree about the principle of זה וזה גורם.

steps.title: The other משנה shows the opposite opinions
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from step 21. In the משנה about destroying an idol, רבי יוסי allows grinding it and scattering it. The רבנן forbid this because the dust becomes fertilizer, and the תורה forbids any benefit from an idol.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we hear them say the opposite? We learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי says, a person grinds up the idol and scatters it to the wind or throws it into the sea. The רבנן said to him: even that becomes fertilizer, and the פסוק says, 'Nothing of the banned things shall cling to your hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a different משנה where רבי יוסי seems lenient about fertilizer from an idol and the רבנן seem strict. That is the opposite of what we just said about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 21 the גמרא pictured רבי יוסי as the strict one about fertilizer from an אשרה and the רבנן as lenient. In the idol משנה, the רבנן worry that the scattered dust will fertilize fields, so they are the strict ones. רבי יוסי is not bothered by it, so he is the lenient one.

keyTerms.meaning: Something banned; here, items connected to idol worship that you may not benefit from

phrases.english: But didn't we hear them say the opposite?
phrases.notes: 'Them' means רבי יוסי and the רבנן from our משנה.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יוסי says:
He grinds it up and scatters it to the wind
or throws it into the sea.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אַף הִיא נַעֲשָׂה זֶבֶל,
phrases.english: They said to him: Even that becomes fertilizer,
and it says: 'Nothing shall cling to your hand'
'of the banned things.'
phrases.notes: דברים 13:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the way step 21 assigned the strict and lenient positions.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that רבי יוסי is strict about fertilizer from forbidden things and the רבנן are lenient.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה shows the רבנן forbidding fertilizer from an idol and רבי יוסי allowing it. That is the reverse of our משנה.

steps.title: Both sides now contradict themselves
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem. The רבנן's opinion here clashes with their opinion there, and רבי יוסי's opinion here clashes with his opinion there.
steps.simpleTranslation: So the רבנן contradict the רבנן, and רבי יוסי contradicts רבי יוסי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states the challenge clearly: each side seems to say one thing in one משנה and the opposite in the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a double contradiction. In our משנה the רבנן are lenient and רבי יוסי is strict. In the idol משנה the רבנן are strict and רבי יוסי is lenient. Each contradiction needs its own answer.

keyTerms.meaning: There is a contradiction between one statement of this person and another statement of the same person
The Sages, meaning the majority opinion

phrases.english: There is a contradiction between the רבנן and the רבנן,
and a contradiction between רבי יוסי and רבי יוסי!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the challenge from step 22 into a formal double contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: The consistency of both רבי יוסי and the רבנן across the two משניות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each side is strict in one משנה and lenient in the other about fertilizer from something forbidden.

steps.title: רבי יוסי's two opinions can be explained
steps.stepSummary: The idol dust gets scattered and disappears, so רבי יוסי permits it. The אשרה leaves do not disappear, so he forbids planting under them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, רבי יוסי against רבי יוסי is not a problem. There, the dust is going to get lost, so he permits it. Here, the leaves are not going to get lost, so it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers half of the challenge by showing that רבי יוסי's two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Scattered idol dust is spread out to the wind or the sea and is basically destroyed. Leaves falling from an אשרה pile right onto the vegetables and fertilize them directly. So רבי יוסי can be strict in one case and lenient in the other without contradicting himself.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this one is fine (the other part is still a problem)
There (the other משנה) and here (our משנה)

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא:
phrases.english: Granted, רבי יוסי against רבי יוסי is not a problem:
There, since it is going to get lost, he permits it;
phrases.notes: 'There' is the ground-up idol dust that is scattered and blown away.

phrases.english: here, since it is not going to get lost, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'Here' is the leaves falling from the אשרה onto the vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אַדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the רבי יוסי half of the double contradiction from step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי seemed lenient about fertilizer in one place and strict in the other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cases differ: dust that is destroyed is permitted, while leaves that stay and fertilize directly are forbidden.

steps.title: The רבנן are still a problem, so swap the names
steps.stepSummary: The difference between the cases does not save the רבנן. If they forbid even scattered dust that gets lost, they should surely forbid leaves that fertilize directly. So the גמרא reverses the names in our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the רבנן against the רבנן is still a problem. So reverse the names.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the רבנן's contradiction cannot be explained, so it fixes it by switching who said what in our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן are strict even about dust that gets lost, so it makes no sense for them to be lenient about leaves that do not get lost. Reversing the names means that in our משנה the רבנן forbid planting vegetables under an אשרה even in the rainy season, and רבי יוסי permits it. Now both sides fit both משניות.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it; swap the names of who said each opinion

steps.whatToRemember: The difference 'goes to waste vs. does not go to waste' explains רבי יוסי but not the רבנן. So the גמרא swaps the names in our משנה. The result: the רבנן forbid planting vegetables under an אשרה even in the rainy season, and רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.confusionAlert: The swap is only in our משנה about the אשרה, not in the idol משנה. The opinions in the idol משנה stay as they are.

phrases.english: But the רבנן against the רבנן is still a problem,
phrases.notes: The רבנן forbid even dust that gets lost, so they should surely forbid leaves that do not.

phrases.english: so reverse it.
phrases.notes: Swap the names in our משנה, so the רבנן are the strict ones and רבי יוסי is lenient.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Admits that the answer in step 24 does not work for the רבנן, then fixes the problem by reversing the names.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן permit vegetables under an אשרה in the rainy season, and רבי יוסי forbids them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן forbid planting even in the rainy season, and רבי יוסי permits it. This matches the idol משנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the גמרא will change which name goes with which opinion in a משנה so the Sages stay consistent across different משניות.

steps.title: Second answer: keep the names, gain is cancelled by loss
steps.stepSummary: Instead of switching the names in the משנה, the גמרא answers each side separately. רבי יוסי is explained as before. The רבנן are explained with רב מרי בריה דרב כהנא's rule: what improves the hide damages the flesh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if you prefer, say: Do not switch the names. רבי יוסי's clash is settled the way we already answered. The רבנן's clash is settled with what רב מרי the son of רב כהנא said: what makes the hide better makes the meat worse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to the clash from step 23. This answer does not change the names in our משנה. Here it brings the rule it will use to explain the רבנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 said the רבנן could not be saved, so it switched the names. Now the גמרא says the רבנן can be saved after all. A gain that comes together with an equal loss is not counted as a real gain. The next step applies this to the אשרה.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces a second, alternative answer
Do not reverse: keep the names in the משנה as they are

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not replace the answer for רבי יוסי from step 24. It keeps that answer and adds a new answer only for the רבנן.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Do not reverse [the names],
phrases.notes: This goes back to step 25, where the גמרא switched רבי יוסי and the רבנן in our משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei's [clash] is as we answered,
phrases.notes: That is step 24: idol dust scatters and is lost, but the אשרה leaves stay.

phrases.english: the Rabbis' [clash] is as said
Rav Mari, son of Rav Kahana:
what improves the hide
phrases.notes: He said this about a sacrificial animal that became unfit. Skinning the hide whole raises its value but cuts up the meat.

phrases.english: damages the flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer instead of the name switch in step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Second answer using a general rule that cancels a gain against a loss
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן must forbid planting under the אשרה, since they forbid even scattered idol dust, so the names had to be switched
steps.terutzMaskana: The names stay as they are. The רבנן permit planting because there is no overall gain, as in רב מרי's rule

steps.title: Applying the rule: the leaves help, the shade harms
steps.stepSummary: The fallen leaves of the אשרה fertilize the plants, but its shade hurts them. The two cancel out, so there is no benefit from the אשרה, and the רבנן permit planting under it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, whatever the foliage adds, the shade takes away.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא applies רב מרי's rule to planting under the אשרה. This finishes the second answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid the idol dust because it is pure benefit. Under the אשרה, the gain from the leaves is cancelled by the harm of the shade. With no overall benefit, the רבנן can permit it without contradicting themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: Fallen leaves or foliage of the tree
Here too: applies an earlier rule to the present case

steps.whatToRemember: Second answer: the names stay. רבי יוסי is settled by the difference between scattered and remaining. The רבנן are settled because the leaves' benefit is cancelled by the shade.

phrases.english: Here too,
what improves through the foliage,
damages through the shade.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule brought in step 26 to the אשרה case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the rule to the case: the benefit cancels out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The leaves under the אשרה give a real benefit, like the idol dust
steps.terutzMaskana: The shade cancels the benefit of the leaves, so the רבנן can permit planting

steps.title: Does רבי יוסי really forbid when two causes combine? The ערלה nut
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי יוסי holds זה וזה גורם אסור. It quotes his teaching about ערלה: one may plant a branch of ערלה, but not a nut of ערלה, because it is a fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי יוסי really hold that when this and that cause something together, it is forbidden? But it is taught: רבי יוסי says, one may plant a branch of ערלה, but one may not plant a nut of ערלה, because it is a fruit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to the idea from step 21 that רבי יוסי forbids when a forbidden and a permitted cause combine. It quotes a teaching of his that sets up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The quoted teaching alone does not yet prove anything. The nut is forbidden to plant simply because planting it uses forbidden fruit. The real problem comes in the next step, with what רב says רבי יוסי admits.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that cause it: a forbidden cause and a permitted cause together produce a result
Fruit of a tree in its first three years, forbidden to eat or benefit from
A branch or shoot cut for planting

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yosei hold
that when this and that cause it, it is forbidden?
But isn't it taught:
Rabbi Yosei says:
One may plant a branch of ערלה,
but one may not plant a nut of ערלה,
because it is a fruit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם אָסוּר? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the claim in step 21 that רבי יוסי forbids when two causes combine. That claim still holds under the 'do not reverse' answer of steps 26-27, and this step begins challenging it from another source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds זה וזה גורם אסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A teaching about ערלה will show רבי יוסי permitting a result that a forbidden and a permitted cause produced together

steps.title: רב: רבי יוסי admits that what grows is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה reports in the name of רב that רבי יוסי admits: if someone already planted, layered, or grafted with ערלה, the result is permitted. What grows comes from both the forbidden nut and the permitted soil, yet רבי יוסי permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said in the name of רב: רבי יוסי admits that if someone planted, layered, or grafted, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This completes the challenge. רבי יוסי permits what grows from ערלה after the fact, which looks like זה וזה גורם מותר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new plant grows from two causes: the forbidden ערלה, and the permitted ground. If רבי יוסי held זה וזה גורם אסור, he would forbid it. Since he permits it, he seems to hold זה וזה גורם מותר, which contradicts step 21.

keyTerms.meaning: Layered: bent a branch into the ground so it takes root

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי still forbids planting the nut to begin with. He permits only what grows once it has already been planted.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
Rabbi Yosei admits
that if one planted, layered, or grafted
phrases.notes: Layering means bending a branch down into the soil so it grows roots of its own.

phrases.english: it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 28
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוסי holds זה וזה גורם אסור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: What grows comes from both the forbidden ערלה and the permitted soil, yet רבי יוסי permits it, so he seems to hold זה וזה גורם מותר

steps.title: A ברייתא also teaches that רבי יוסי admits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a ברייתא that says the same as רב: רבי יוסי admits. The rest of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it is also taught this way: רבי יוסי admits...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a support for רב's report from a ברייתא. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Backing up רב with a ברייתא makes the challenge stronger. It is not just one אמורא's report; a ברייתא also says that רבי יוסי permits what grows.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is also taught so: a ברייתא that supports what was just said

phrases.english: And it is also taught so:
Rabbi Yosei admits

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: מוֹדֶה רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's report from step 29 with a ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: רב's report that רבי יוסי permits what grows from ערלה after it was planted, layered, or grafted
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא stating that רבי יוסי admits
